newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday January 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday January 22.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The Bank of Italy cut its official discount rate to 6.75 percent from 7.50 percent, the lowest level since September 1975. The central bank said it acted following a steady decline in inflation in recent months but added it would continue to watch closely trends in consumer demand, labour costs and price policies (all).

* The ruling coalition reached agreement with hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which guarantees the government's majority in the lower house of parliament, over measures to boost the car market, but they could not reach a common position on the sell-off of state telecom giant Stet (all).
* The lower house is expected to approve today the set-up of a bi-cameral commission to carry out constitutional reforms (all).
* January consumer prices are seen at 0.2 percent month on month and 2.6 percent year on year, according to estimates based on preliminary data from 11 sample cities.

*Information technology group Olivetti rose 2.6 percent on the Milan stock exchange market in the first day after the announced sale of its ailing PC division to a group of domestic and international investors led bu US lawyer Edward Gottesman. In an interview Olivetti's CEO Roberto Colaninno says negotiations are also "at a good point" with France Telecom over a planned joint venture with telecom services unit Infostrada (Corriere della Sera).

* Sergio Siglienti, chairman of insurer INA, says its group should not maintain a position of control in Banco di Napoli once the privatisation process is over. On January 18, the Treasury accepted a joint bid by Ina and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro to take a 60 percent stake in the struggling southern bank. In the bid, Ina would take 51 percent of the firm and BNL 49 percent (Corriere della Sera).
* Early 1997 data point to a worse-than-expected public sector deficit this year underlining the need for a hefty mini-budget, according to an unsourced report (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
